name: Deliver as 'One Arm'
definition: Understand the connections and complexities beyond your function. Collaboration isn't always consensus.

rows.under: Stays inside the function. Treats other groups as someone else's problem.
rows.justRight: Learns how the work connects beyond their function. Names the dependencies and the tradeoffs before they become surprises.
rows.over: Inserts themselves into every other function's work. Creates meetings instead of connections.

rows.under: Pretends the path is simple when it is not. Hides the hard parts from partners.
rows.justRight: Surfaces the real complexities early, including the ones that sit outside their team. Helps others see the whole picture.
rows.over: Uses complexity as a reason to stall. Makes the work sound harder than it is.

rows.under: Either goes it alone or waits until everyone agrees.
rows.justRight: Collaborates to understand the connections, then moves when the decision is clear. Does not confuse alignment with unanimous agreement.
rows.over: Forces a vote on every detail. Treats dissent as a veto.

rows.under: Throws work over the wall. Does not check whether the next team can actually take it.
rows.justRight: Hands work off with the context the next team needs. Stays available until the connection holds.
rows.over: Never lets go. Sits in every other team's review so nothing moves without them.

rows.situation: A local win that hurts another team
rows.under: Optimizes the function and ignores the cost to the company.
rows.justRight: Chooses the outcome that works for Arm, even when it is harder for their own group.
rows.over: Sacrifices their team's real work to appear collaborative. Becomes a bottleneck for everyone else's priorities.
